statement_en:
Let \(F(s,x):\\mathbb{R}^2\	o\\mathbb{R}\) be real analytic in some neighborhood \(U\) of \((s^{*},x_k(0))\), and suppose
\\[
F(s^{*},x_k(0))=0,\\quad F_x(s^{*},x_k(0))\
eq 0.
\\]
Then there exist a neighborhood \(V\) of \(s^{*}\) and a neighborhood \(W\) of \(x_k(0)\) such that on \(V\) the equation \(F(s,x)=0\) has exactly one solution branch
\\[
x(s):V\	o W,
\\]
and \(x(s)\) is real analytic, namely
\\[
x(s)=\\sum_{i\\ge 0} a_i s^i,\\quad \\forall s\\in V.
\\]
final_code:
import Mathlib

theorem analytic_implicit_function_solution_branch
    {F : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ} {sStar x0 : ℝ}
    (h_analytic : AnalyticAt ℝ (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => F p.1 p.2) (sStar, x0))
    (h_zero : F sStar x0 = 0)
    (h_deriv : deriv (fun x => F sStar x) x0 ≠ 0) :
    ∃ V W : Set ℝ,
      IsOpen V ∧ IsOpen W ∧ sStar ∈ V ∧ x0 ∈ W ∧
      ∃ x : ℝ → ℝ,
        (∀ s ∈ V, x s ∈ W) ∧
        (∀ s ∈ V, F s (x s) = 0) ∧
        (∀ s ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ W, F s y = 0 → y = x s) ∧
        (∀ s ∈ V, AnalyticAt ℝ x s) ∧
        ∃ a : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ s ∈ V, HasSum (fun i : ℕ => a i * s ^ i) (x s) := by
  sorry
